nodes.title: Upsampler system prompt
widgets_values:
You are the prompt upsampler of an image-editing model. You see the reference image(s), attached in order (the first image, the second image, ...), and the user's short request. Expand it into ONE detailed, self-contained instruction: the caption the editing model receives together with the same images. Output only the instruction as one continuous English prose block, with no greetings, explanations, Markdown, JSON, coordinates, ids or angle-bracket tokens. Read a vague or conversational request as the most plausible edit of the supplied images.

Pick the voice by task shape. When one reference stays and gets bounded changes, write an imperative editing instruction on it ("Remove the ...", "Change the ... to ...", "Zoom in on ..."); a whole-image transformation opens with its scope ("Convert the entire image into ...", "Apply a ... filter over the entire scene", "Horizontally flip the entire image so that ...", "Shift the camera viewpoint to ...", then where the major elements should now be). When the references are drawn into a newly composed frame (combining subjects, a new scene, a garment, object or style donor), write a generation request ("Create a photograph of ...", "Create an anime-style illustration of ...", "Generate a new image featuring ...") that says what to take from each image, by ordinal, and what is newly generated.

Keep every explicit edit, constraint, count, position, style cue and piece of wording, and decide what is left open as one concrete plan. Ground everything in what is actually visible: identify each referent unambiguously by its real appearance, never mention content that is not there, and use every image the user attached. State every end state concretely (which color, how large, which pose, which material) and give new content enough appearance to be generated. Cover the knock-on effects of the change (shadows, reflections, occlusion, perspective, scale, lighting) and say what fills a removed region. A zoom-in names what stays in frame and which neighbors are cropped out; an outpainting continues the scene in the same medium. Describe the change, not the whole scene, and close an editing instruction with one compact clause naming what stays unchanged; transferred people keep their identity, face and accessories unless asked otherwise. Transcribe on-image text verbatim in its original language inside double quotes, with line breaks as \n, and match the original font, size and color when replacing it. Name recognizable public figures, brands and landmarks you can see. Directions are frame-relative; use no evaluative or quality words. Typical length is 50 to 150 words.

Output only the instruction.

★ Target video (six-section MiniMax prompt)
widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Video 1> is the source video for the editing task: one continuous 9.4 s handheld take in a small sunlit record shop in which a woman talks to the camera, turns to a crate of records, pulls out a record sleeve, holds it up in front of her face, lowers it, laughs, steps toward the camera and talks to it again in close-up.
<Picture 1> and <Picture 2> are two frames of the target video, <Picture 1> from [Shot 1] at 00:00.500 and <Picture 2> from [Shot 1] at 00:08.750.
<Subject 1> is Walter in <Picture 1> and <Picture 2>: an East Asian man in his mid fifties with short salt-and-pepper hair swept back, a trimmed grey goatee and round tortoiseshell glasses, wearing a navy-blue cotton chore coat buttoned over a grey crew-neck sweater, and charcoal trousers. He replaces the person in <Video 1>, a woman in her early thirties with shoulder-length wavy auburn hair and freckles, wearing a mustard-yellow corduroy jacket over a white T-shirt, a thin silver necklace and dark indigo jeans.

summary:
[video editing + character replacement] The target video is an edited version of <Video 1> in which the woman becomes <Subject 1>, Walter, looking exactly as he does in <Picture 1> and <Picture 2>. The record shop, the crates of vinyl records, the posters, the windows, the warm late-afternoon sunlight and the record sleeve are unchanged. The single continuous shot, the handheld camera, the motion, the timing, the lip movements and every action of <Video 1> are kept. No other character appears.

retention_analysis:
<Video 1> (source video editing): fully_preserved - the single continuous shot [Shot 1] from 00:00.000 to 00:09.417 with no cut, the handheld framing and gentle sway, the record shop with its wooden crates of records, wall posters and large windows, the warm sunlight, the record sleeve with its green cover, and the motion and timing of every head turn, reach, lift, step, laugh and spoken word are copied frame for frame.
<Picture 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): reference - a frame of the target video. Walter standing in the aisle framed from the knees up, his face, head and outfit, and the shop, framing and lighting are taken from <Picture 1>.
<Picture 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): reference - a frame of the target video. Walter in close-up from the chest up holding the record sleeve in both hands, his face, head and outfit, and the shop, framing and lighting are taken from <Picture 2>. The figure in both pictures is the same Walter.
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the salt-and-pepper hair, grey goatee, round tortoiseshell glasses, navy chore coat, grey sweater and charcoal trousers stay identical in every frame, also in profile, while the record sleeve passes in front of the face, and in close-up.

detailed_description:
The target video is a realistic handheld scene in a sunlit independent record shop with warm late-afternoon light, natural colours and fine film grain.
[Shot 1] At 00:00.000 <Subject 1>, Walter, stands in the aisle between wooden crates of vinyl records, framed from the knees up, facing the camera, arms at his sides. At 00:00.500 he is exactly as in <Picture 1>, mouth open as he speaks to the camera. At about 00:01.200 he turns his head into profile toward the crate on the left of frame and looks down at the records, and from about 00:01.800 to 00:03.700 he reaches into the crate with one hand and pulls out a record sleeve. At about 00:04.300 he swings the sleeve up, and from about 00:04.900 to 00:05.700 he holds the record sleeve in both hands in front of his face so that it hides the face completely. At about 00:06.200 he lowers the sleeve to his chest and laughs, facing the camera. From about 00:06.800 he takes two steps toward the camera, and at about 00:07.500 he raises one hand to the side of his head while laughing. From about 00:08.300 he is in close-up from the chest up, holding the sleeve at chest height, and at 00:08.750 he is exactly as in <Picture 2>, speaking to the camera, and at the end he smiles at the camera with closed lips. The camera is handheld throughout.
In every frame, from the first to the last, the person in the shop is this same Walter exactly as in <Picture 1> and <Picture 2>: no auburn hair, no woman's face, no mustard jacket, no white T-shirt, no necklace and no jeans at any moment, also when he is in profile and right after the sleeve is lowered. Only one record sleeve is held. Only this one figure changes, and everything else stays as in <Video 1>.

overall_soundscape:
The source soundtrack continues throughout, with the voice speaking to the camera, a laugh, quiet room tone of the shop and the soft rustle of record sleeves.

nodes.title: ABOUT
widgets_values:
## DUGco Viggle Remake Character Swap (MiniMax H3)
Give it **a shot** and **say who should be in it**. It repaints the person on two frames of your shot, then MiniMax H3 with the Viggle Remake swap LoRA re-shoots the whole clip to match those two frames. The camera, the set, the timing, the lip movement and the soundtrack stay.

**It does three kinds of swap, all from the paint instruction and the prompt**
- **Full recast**: a different person, creature or robot, with their own outfit.
- **Head swap**: new face and hair, same body and clothes.
- **Costume change**: same person, new clothes.

**How to use**
1. **Group 1**: load the shot. It must be 24 fps. Set ★ Length to a valid count (17n + 5: 124, 175, 226, 294) no longer than the clip; 294 frames (12 s) is the recommended ceiling.
2. **Group 3**: pick two frames where the person is clearly visible, one early and one late, ideally a wide and a close view. Write the ★ Paint instruction. Run, and **look at the two keyframes** before trusting the render: they are the identity. If you paint your own frames in another editor, load them and turn on ★ Use my own painted frames.
3. **Group 4**: describe the finished video in the six-section MiniMax format. Name the person as <Subject 1>, say what stays, and walk through the action with times.
4. **Group 5 and 6** render and save. 480 short edge takes about 2.5 minutes for 226 frames on a 96 GB card; 736 takes about 10.5 minutes and is clearly sharper.

**Needs**
- Custom nodes: `ComfyUI-Viggle-Remake` (from the Viggle Remake repository, `comfyui/` folder) and KJNodes (Set/Get).
- Models: MiniMax H3 `fl2va` transformer, the H3 Qwen3-VL text encoder and both H3 VAEs; `viggle_remake_swap_comfyui.safetensors` in `models/loras`; FLUX 3 Klein with its text encoder, VAE and prompt upsampler for the painting step.

**Licence, in plain words**
The Viggle Remake LoRA is a derivative of MiniMax H3 and falls under the **MiniMax H3 Community License**: a commercial product must show "MiniMax H3" in its interface, and a company earning over US$20 million a year needs written permission from MiniMax. Read the licence before you use this for paid work. Use it only on footage you have the right to change, with the consent of the people in it, and label the result as AI-generated.

nodes.title: NOTE
widgets_values: **Your shot.** 24 fps, at least as long as ★ Length. The clip is trimmed to that many frames from its start. Its own sound is kept and drives the lips.

nodes.title: NOTE
widgets_values: **Models.** The LoRA loads through the *bypass* loader on the first/last-frame (`fl2va`) H3 model: that is the pairing Viggle trained for. *Hold keyframes until 0.9* pins the painted frames for the first four of six steps.

nodes.title: NOTE
widgets_values: **Keyframes are the identity.** Each ★ frame number is pulled from your shot and repainted by FLUX 3 Klein. Keyframe 2 is painted with a tight crop of keyframe 1 as its identity picture, so both show the same character: set the ★ Identity crop so it frames the new character (x, y, width, height on a 1280 x 736 frame). Given the whole wide frame, keyframe 2 copies its framing and the render drifts wide. Check both previews: a wrong face here is a wrong face in every frame.

nodes.title: NOTE
widgets_values: **The prompt describes the finished video**, not the edit. Keep the six section names. <Video 1> is your shot, <Picture 1> and <Picture 2> are the keyframes, <Subject 1> is the new character.

nodes.title: NOTE
widgets_values: **Render.** The two frame numbers become the pins, so each keyframe lands on the frame it was painted from. Six euler steps with fixed sigmas; change ★ Seed for another take.

nodes.title: NOTE
widgets_values: **Result.** Picture and the source soundtrack, saved to `output/viggle_remake`.
